entries.title: The public evaluation payload is UNSCANNED for secrets

target.quote: dependency security on all platforms; release/CI with Bun.

entries.corrected_statement: Ticket 09 marks dependency security `not-run` but never says that no secret scan covers the evaluation payload. The payload is UNSCANNED: the branch `eval/issue-2-bun-toolchain`, the 21 detached `eval-bun-ci-*` tag commits and the public Actions artifacts on `slighter12/Navide` have no gitleaks scan receipt in any record examined, and no workflow was triggered to produce one. In all 7 commit/push receipts examined (listed below) the local hook printed that the scan was skipped because gitleaks is not installed, and the hook exits 0 in that case. `.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` triggers (line 3ff.) only on push to `main`/`master`, `pull_request` and manual dispatch, so no workflow scans the eval branch or tags; the fork run listing shows 58 Secret scan runs, all on `main`. Nothing about this evaluation may be described as secret-scan clean. Whether to scan (and where) is a separate user decision; this erratum authorizes and performs no scan.
entries.limits: The examined receipts are the ones listed; I did not enumerate every earlier ticket commit or tag-push receipt (tickets 01-09, 07/08 attempt pushes), so the statement is 'no examined receipt shows a scan that ran' plus the workflow-trigger fact, not a claim about every historical hook invocation. gitleaks absence was observed on the PATH of this worker's shell only. A reviewer's ad-hoc pattern sweep is not equivalent to the pinned gitleaks check (project pin 8.24.3 in secret-scan.yml).

entries.title: Ticket 09 section 7.1: authority attribution and the 'inert on Node' scope

target.quote: All edits fall under the user's 2026-10-11 rule
`setupFiles` entry for the anchor helper + 3 EditorPane mock aliases

entries.corrected_statement: Not all 12 listed paths fall under the user's 2026-10-11 test-adaptation rule. That rule covers only the test-support and test-file edits made under it (on or after 2026-10-11). The Bun manifest and lock, the dispatcher, the vue-tsc launcher, `publicPackagesSetup.ts`, the `test.alias` entries and the two evaluation workflows were initial evaluation-toolchain configuration under the evaluation's own authority (ticket 02 allowlist and review, ticket 03 startup, tickets 07/08 and ci-refresh-01 dispatches); their commits predate the rule or were dispatched separately (attribution tables below, by commit). 'Inert on Node' holds for the helper's *effects*, not for its loading: `tests/support/bunMockImporterAnchor.ts` is registered through `setupFiles` for every runtime, so on Node the module is still imported and evaluated (imports, function definitions, `ownFile` at line 45). Both mutations are gated by `isBun` (line 43): the `vi.mock`/`unmock`/`doMock`/`doUnmock`/`importActual`/`importMock` wrapping (line 90) and the `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` assignment (line 112). This is by reading the code; it was not re-measured here. The three `test.alias` entries in `vitest.config.ts` (line 48) are NOT Bun-gated and apply to Node runs; they match only the exact specifiers `./view/EditorViewMonaco.vue`, `../foundation` and `../shared`, which at HEAD occur only in `packages/plugin-ui/src/editor/EditorPane.test.ts`, `packages/plugin-ui/src/editor/EditorPane.vue` (scan receipt). That is harmless today but fragile for any future file using those specifiers.
entries.limits: Attribution is by commit date and dispatch text; it does not re-judge any edit and changes no conclusion about the amount of adaptation. Commit ids are the post-rebase ids at HEAD.

entries.title: Windows root-cold performance: robustness of the verdict with two exit-1 Node samples

target.quote: 2 Node root-cold samples exited 1 (worker RPC timeout) and stay in the median
Windows Node root-cold has 2 of 5 samples that exited 1

entries.corrected_statement: Recomputed from the raw receipt (5 measured pairs after the warm-up; Node = `base`): Node samples 640.469, 646.812, 665.062, 727.422, 753.468 s, of which the two exit-1 samples are 727.422, 753.468 s; Bun samples 372.109, 375.797, 405.422, 425.016, 426.75 s (all exit 1: the accepted `pluginExternalWorkspace` residual). Medians Node 665.062 s / Bun 405.422 s (-39.04%), as in the report. The verdict is robust to the two failed Node samples: Bun's slowest sample (426.75 s) is faster than Node's fastest (640.469 s) by 213.72 s (worst-case pairing -33.37%), so no pairing of the recorded samples approaches the +10% gate. The two exit-1 Node samples are the two slowest Node samples and the Node median (665.062 s) is itself an exit-0 sample; with them excluded the Node median of the remaining three would be 646.812 s and the ratio -37.32% (arithmetic on the same samples, not a new measurement). This supports 'no observed Bun slowdown above the gate'. It does not make the -39.0% a clean five-pair speedup magnitude (unequal successful-work coverage: two Node samples exit 1, all Bun samples exit 1), and it does not relabel the failures or imply a passing Windows correctness gate; the two failed samples stay disclosed and stay in the median as reported.
entries.limits: Single hosted-runner attempt (one run); no extra samples were taken, as the dispatch forbids measurements. Warm-up pair excluded as in the report.
